reviewer: OpenAI R3-83 Mega-first vertical wave 6 (10-species batch) audit
notes: Review is scoped to the 12-Pokémon Beta 2 slice.
The six original beta Pokémon remain the starter team; the other six enter through Roster Ranch.
Regular Roster M-A provides a captured pull count of 10; Vanguard economy costs remain explicit local-beta configuration.
Beta v3 adds reviewed Sunny Day, Rain Dance, Chlorophyll, Rain Dish, Heat Rock and Damp Rock as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks 5/8-turn weather, 1.5/0.5 damage, doubled weather Speed and Rain Dish 1/16 recovery.
Beta v4 adds reviewed Tailwind, Reflect, Light Screen and Light Clay as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Tailwind duration/Speed, screen duration/damage modifiers, critical bypass and Light Clay extension.
Beta v5 adds reviewed Grassy Terrain, Misty Terrain and Terrain Extender as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.

Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks five-turn terrain, Terrain Extender eight-turn duration, Grassy grounded healing/Grass boost/quake-like reduction, and Misty grounded status/confusion protection plus Dragon damage reduction.

Grounding support for this slice covers Flying types and the already-modelled Magnet Rise/Telekinesis volatile flags; Levitate, Air Balloon, Gravity and other grounding overrides remain blocked for future mechanics batches.
Beta v6 adds reviewed Spikes for Chesnaught and Stealth Rock for Infernape as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Spikes at 1/8, 1/6 and 1/4 max HP for grounded switch-ins, plus Stealth Rock at Rock effectiveness × 1/8 max HP.
Hazards share the R3-20 entry/replacement lifecycle. Heavy-Duty Boots, hazard removal, Magic Guard and additional grounding overrides remain fail-closed until their own reviewed batches.
Showdown sim/battle.ts cross-checks tied SwitchIn side-condition handlers resolving by stable creation effectOrder.
Beta v7 adds reviewed Rapid Spin for Blastoise and Defog for Decidueye/Scizor as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Rapid Spin cleanup only after a successful damaging hit, removal of Leech Seed and user-side entry hazards, plus a +1 Speed secondary boost.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Defog lowering target Evasion, removing Reflect/Light Screen from the target side, clearing supported entry hazards from both sides, and clearing active terrain.
Beta v8 adds reviewed Toxic Spikes for Beedrill as an optional Training choice; default builds remain unchanged.

Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Toxic Spikes at two layers: grounded entrants receive poison at one layer or bad poison at two layers; grounded Poison types absorb the condition, while Steel and ungrounded targets are unaffected.

Rapid Spin and Defog cleanup now include Toxic Spikes in the pinned Showdown hazard-removal order. Heavy-Duty Boots, Magic Guard, Sticky Web, Court Change and additional grounding overrides remain fail-closed.
Beta v9 promotes reviewed Wonder Room for Primarina as an optional Training choice; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Room duration at five turns and same-Room recast toggling the pseudo-weather off rather than refreshing it.
Wonder Room swaps Defense and Sp. Def base stats before applying the stage modifier for the requested defensive stat.
Trick Room and Magic Room core mechanics are implemented and regression-tested but remain unavailable in Beta v9 because none of the 12 reviewed species has a legal M-A relation to those moves.

Trick Room uses priority -7 and dynamic reversed Speed ordering within an action priority bracket; Magic Room suppresses held-item passive effects while leaving Ability effects and Mega evolution eligibility outside that suppression contract.
Beta v10 promotes reviewed Yawn for Blastoise and Perish Song for Primarina as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.

Pinned Showdown/Champions evidence cross-checks Yawn as a two-residual delayed sleep: protection and grounded Electric Terrain block scheduling, while sleep immunity/status rules are rechecked when the delayed effect resolves.

Perish Song assigns an initial perish count of 4 to each currently active eligible Pokémon, decrements at the end of every turn including the use turn, faints at count 0 without damage, and switching clears the counter.

The shared delayed-effect scheduler resolves after existing end-turn HP residual groups and before ordinary field/condition expiry, preserves deterministic RNG, and stores delayed state on the affected Pokémon so ordinary switching removes it.
Soundproof/Baton Pass transfer semantics and Future Sight-style delayed attacks remain fail-closed outside the completed delayed-effect family.
Beta v11 promotes reviewed Solar Beam, Solar Blade, Hydro Cannon, Frenzy Plant, Blast Burn, Hyper Beam and Giga Impact as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Solar Beam/Solar Blade as two-turn charge attacks that skip preparation in sun; the currently supported Rain weather halves their released base power. Sand/snow-specific power modifiers remain outside the active weather family.

The charge commitment spends PP on preparation, locks the same move and target for release, does not spend PP again on release, and is cleared when the committed release is prevented before execution.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Hydro Cannon, Frenzy Plant, Blast Burn, Hyper Beam and Giga Impact using the must-recharge condition after a successful damaging use; the following action is an automatic recharge turn.
Dig, Fly, Dive, Phantom Force and other semi-invulnerable two-turn moves remain fail-closed until their hit-through exceptions and semi-invulnerability contracts are implemented and reviewed.
Beta v12 promotes reviewed Dig, Fly, Dive and Phantom Force as optional Training choices through real M-A learnset relations; default builds remain unchanged.
Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Dig as underground on preparation: ordinary attacks fail, Earthquake/Magnitude hit through and receive a 2x damage modifier.
Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Dive as underwater on preparation: ordinary attacks fail, Surf/Whirlpool hit through and receive a 2x damage modifier.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Fly as airborne on preparation: Gust/Twister/Sky Uppercut/Thunder/Hurricane/Smack Down/Thousand Arrows hit through, Gust/Twister receive 2x damage, and Smack Down interrupts the Fly commitment after connecting.
Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Phantom Force as vanished during preparation and as bypassing/breaking Protect on release.
The shared two-turn commitment still spends PP only on preparation, locks move plus target for release, and clears the semi-invulnerable state before the release attack resolves.

Gravity/Bounce/Sky Drop and unreviewed exception-move secondary mechanics remain fail-closed; the shared resolver only claims hit-through, 2x semi-invulnerability damage and the reviewed Smack Down interruption contract.

Beta v13 promotes reviewed Solar Power, Leaf Guard, Flash Fire, Sniper, Technician, Iron Fist, Bulletproof, Long Reach and Liquid Voice through real M-A Ability relations; default builds remain unchanged.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Solar Power sun Sp. Atk boost plus 1/8 max-HP residual, Leaf Guard sun status/Yawn blocking, Flash Fire Fire immunity plus persistent 1.5x Fire offensive boost until switch, and Sniper critical-damage amplification.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Technician base-power threshold <=60, Iron Fist punch-tag boost, Bulletproof bullet-tag immunity, Long Reach contact suppression and Liquid Voice sound-tag conversion to Water.

Move tags are validated mechanics data rather than Ability-specific move-name lists. Beta v13 tags Bullet Seed as bullet, Drain Punch as punch, Sing/Perish Song/Hyper Voice as sound, and promotes Hyper Voice for Primarina so Liquid Voice has an active damaging interaction.
Beta v14 adds a shared post-damage secondary-effect framework and promotes Feraligatr's real M-A Sheer Force relation.
Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Sheer Force by removing move secondaries and applying the 5325/4096 base-power modifier when a move has secondary effects.
Beta v14 promotes Waterfall, Crunch, Liquidation, Ice Punch, Body Slam, Rock Slide, Water Pulse, Ice Fang and Bulldoze as reviewed Feraligatr Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.

Secondary effects resolve only for targets that actually took move damage, roll independently per target/effect using authoritative seeded RNG, and reuse the existing major-status, volatile-status and stat-stage state rules.

Ice Fang validates multiple independent secondaries; Rock Slide validates per-target spread rolls; Bulldoze validates a 100% secondary and all-adjacent spread behavior. Sheer Force suppresses all of these secondary effects while preserving the power boost.
Ability suppression/copy/swap/replacement and Light Metal remain fail-closed for later R3.8 waves; Light Metal still waits for canonical species weight data.
Beta v15 promotes reviewed Leftovers, Sitrus Berry and Focus Sash from the Champions candidate item pool; default builds remain unchanged.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Leftovers restoring 1/16 max HP at end turn, Sitrus Berry activating at half HP or lower to restore 1/4 max HP and then being consumed, and Focus Sash preserving a full-HP holder at 1 HP from otherwise lethal move damage before being consumed.

The shared held-item state now owns reveal, activation, consumption and idempotent activation receipts. Consumed items remain consumed after JSON restart/replay state serialization and cannot reactivate.

Opponent/AI projections keep unrevealed held items hidden and expose the item only after an authoritative reveal event. Magic Room suppresses the active held-item hook without consuming or revealing the item.
Item loss/swap/steal, berries beyond Sitrus, status-curing items, Choice lock and other survival/recovery items remain fail-closed until their own reviewed R3.9 waves.
Beta v16 promotes reviewed Lum Berry, Cheri Berry, Chesto Berry, Pecha Berry, Rawst Berry, Aspear Berry and Persim Berry from the Champions candidate item pool; default builds remain unchanged.

PokéBase Champions descriptions define Lum Berry as curing any major status or confusion; Cheri/Chesto/Pecha/Rawst/Aspear cure paralysis/sleep/poison/burn/freeze and Persim cures confusion. Pecha also clears the engine bad-poison state as the toxic form of poison.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks status berries as on-update consumables and Lum as curing both a major status and confusion when present. The shared item-status-cure hook consumes exactly once and emits authoritative reveal/activation/consume plus cure events.

Magic Room suppresses status-cure berries without revealing or consuming them. Natural Magic Room expiry and recast toggle-off run a post-suppression item update before the next action-order-sensitive turn, so a stored paralysis/sleep/freeze cannot incorrectly gate the following action.
Beta v17 promotes reviewed Life Orb, Rocky Helmet and Shell Bell from the Champions candidate item pool; default builds remain unchanged.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Life Orb with a 5324/4096 damage modifier for damaging moves and 1/10 max-HP recoil after a qualifying damaging move. Sheer Force keeps the Life Orb damage modifier while suppressing the AfterMoveSecondarySelf recoil path.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Rocky Helmet dealing 1/6 of the contact attacker max HP per damaging contact hit, including when the holder faints from that hit. Long Reach contact removal prevents the retaliation and Magic Room suppresses the item without revealing it.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Shell Bell healing 1/8 of aggregate move damage in its after-move self phase. Spread and multi-hit damage therefore aggregate into one recovery amount; Sheer Force and force-switch moves skip that after-move self hook.

The shared post-damage item pipeline resolves native recoil/drain/recharge first, then Life Orb/Shell Bell at order 145, before pivot/forced-switch handlers at order 150. Rocky Helmet remains per-hit inside the direct damage resolver so multi-hit contact can retaliate on each successful hit and stop later hits if the attacker faints.
Beta v18 promotes reviewed Choice Scarf from the Champions candidate item pool; default builds remain unchanged.

PokéBase Champions defines Choice Scarf as a 50% Speed boost that restricts the holder to the first move it uses until it switches out. Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks a 1.5x Speed modifier plus the shared choicelock condition.

Choice lock is established only after the before-action gate allows the move attempt, is serialized in the holder volatile state, and is cleared by the shared switch lifecycle. Switching remains legal while locked.

Magic Room suppresses both the Choice Scarf Speed modifier and command restriction without deleting the stored lock; when suppression ends the prior lock becomes active again, matching the pinned item-ignore contract. The passive effect does not reveal the opponent held item by itself.

At the Wave 4 checkpoint, Choice Band/Choice Specs were not present in the current beta2 candidate snapshot, so only Choice Scarf was promoted while the shared lock contract stayed reusable. Resistance berries, White Herb, item loss/swap/steal and Heavy-Duty Boots were still fail-closed at that checkpoint.
Beta v19 promotes reviewed White Herb from the Champions candidate item pool; default builds remain unchanged.

PokéBase Champions defines White Herb as restoring the holder’s lowered stats to normal and consuming after use. The shared item-negative-stage-reset hook clears every negative battle stage to zero while preserving non-negative stages and consumes exactly once after a qualifying stat-lowering event.

White Herb resolution is shared across primary stat-stage handlers, secondary stat drops and supported protection retaliation. Magic Room suppresses activation without reveal/consumption; recast or natural expiry releases the stored negative stages, while JSON restart state is repaired on the normal before-action item update.

At the Beta v19 checkpoint, resistance berries, item loss/swap/steal and Heavy-Duty Boots remained fail-closed for later R3.9 waves. Light Metal remained blocked pending canonical species weight data.
Beta v20 promotes the complete Champions candidate resistance-berry family: 17 typed super-effective berries plus Chilan Berry for the first damaging Normal-type hit. Default builds remain unchanged.

The shared item-resist-hit hook runs only after a move has passed targeting/protection/accuracy into the direct damage path. Typed berries require matching move type plus effectiveness above 1; Chilan explicitly does not require super effectiveness. The item is revealed and consumed before damage and contributes one 0.5 damage modifier to that hit.

Multi-hit attacks consume the berry on the first qualifying hit, so later hits are unmodified. Magic Room suppresses activation without reveal/consumption, and serialized consumed state prevents reactivation after restart/replay.

Beta v20 also fills the nine missing canonical 20% type-boost held items using the existing held-damage-boost contract: Black Glasses, Hard Stone, Magnet, Never-Melt Ice, Poison Barb, Silk Scarf, Soft Sand, Spell Tag and Twisted Spoon.

Expert Belt uses the same passive damage pipeline with a super-effective selector and boosts qualifying damaging hits by 20%. Wide Lens adds a passive 10% accuracy multiplier after accuracy/evasion stages, capped at 100%. Neither passive effect reveals the held item merely by modifying a calculation; Magic Room suppresses both.

Oran Berry reuses the authoritative HP-threshold consumable contract at half HP or lower but restores a fixed 10 HP instead of a max-HP fraction. Reveal, consume, idempotency, residual/hazard timing and Magic Room behavior remain shared with Sitrus Berry.

Higher-risk item families that require grounding, forced switching, PP restoration, species-gated critical-ratio interactions, move-level spread receipts, item transfer/loss or trapping remain fail-closed rather than being inferred into this batch. Light Metal remains blocked pending canonical species weight data.

Beta v20 additionally promotes Bright Powder on the shared accuracy pipeline: incoming move accuracy is multiplied by 0.9 after accuracy/evasion stages; it remains a passive hidden modifier and Magic Room suppresses it without revealing the item.

Scope Lens adds a generic item-critical-ratio stage. The direct-damage critical roll now derives its chance from the holder critical stage (base 1/24; +1 = 1/8; +2 = 1/2; +3 = guaranteed), with Magic Room suppressing held-item stages and no passive reveal.

Focus Band reuses item-survive-lethal-hit with requireFullHp=false, a seeded 10% activation roll and consume=false. The chance is checked only for otherwise lethal move damage, including fixed-damage handlers; successful activation reveals but preserves the item so later lethal hits may roll again.

Beta v21 promotes 17 reviewed item mechanics without changing any default build: Air Balloon, Big Root, four terrain Seeds, Iron Ball, Leppa Berry, Normal Gem, Red Card, Zoom Lens, King's Rock, Metronome, Light Ball, Leek, Mental Herb and Quick Claw.

Pinned Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Air Balloon Ground/hazard immunity and damaging-hit pop, Iron Ball grounding/Speed reduction, terrain-seed stat activation, Leppa Berry 10 PP restoration, Normal Gem one-shot Normal power, Red Card attacker phazing, Big Root drain/Leech Seed healing, and Zoom Lens post-target accuracy. These share authoritative held-item activation, Magic Room suppression and restart-safe state rather than item-specific battle branches.

King's Rock adds one seeded 10% post-damage flinch roll only to damaging moves without their own flinch secondary and is suppressed with Sheer Force secondary suppression. Metronome stores a switch-cleared consecutive-move chain from 1.0x through a 2.0x cap. Light Ball doubles Pikachu Attack and Sp. Atk through species-gated stat hooks; Leek adds two critical-ratio stages to Farfetch'd/Sirfetch'd; Mental Herb consumes once to clear supported restrictive volatile state and resolves deferred state when Magic Room ends.

Quick Claw uses a dedicated deterministic turn-order preparation hook rather than an ad-hoc priority increase: each holder move rolls once per turn, a success acts before ordinary Speed/Trick Room ordering only inside the same move-priority bracket, and higher-priority moves remain ahead. The item is revealed on successful activation, is not consumed, and Magic Room suppresses the roll.

Eject Button remains fail-closed until a mid-turn replacement-choice lifecycle can suspend, collect a legal replacement and resume without allowing the ejected holder to replace itself. Binding Band and Shed Shell remain blocked on trapping/Bound foundations; Icy Rock and Smooth Rock remain blocked until Snow and Sandstorm weather families are implemented. Light Metal remains blocked pending canonical species weight data.
Beta v22 promotes reviewed Sandstorm for Charizard/Scizor, Snowscape for Primarina, plus Icy Rock and Smooth Rock as optional Training content; default builds remain unchanged.

The shared weather engine now models Snow's 1.5x Defense for Ice types, Sandstorm's 1.5x Sp. Def for Rock types, Sandstorm 1/16 residual damage with Rock/Ground/Steel immunity, and eight-turn duration rocks.

Sand Rush, Slush Rush, Ice Body, Sand Force, Sand Veil and Snow Cloak are mechanics-supported in both formats but remain outside Beta v22 because none of the 12 reviewed beta species has a legal M-A Ability relation to them. This preserves relation-gated content promotion while retaining reusable engine support.

Eject Button remains fail-closed pending mid-turn replacement choice/resume semantics. Binding Band and Shed Shell remain blocked on trapping foundations; Light Metal remains blocked pending canonical species weight data.

Beta v23 keeps the v22 roster and enabled IDs unchanged while refreshing promoted mechanics from the current reviewed manifests; this carries machine-readable move tags such as pulse into runtime for newly promoted Mega abilities such as Mega Launcher.
R3-78 Mega forms and Mega Stones remain a separate mega-beta-v2 extension; they do not expand ordinary Training species or default builds.
Beta v24 expands the ordinary playable catalog only with four M-A species that each have a promoted Mega relation in R3-80: Steelix, Camerupt, Heracross and Medicham.
Their default builds intentionally reuse already-reviewed moves/items; only Solid Rock and Pure Power are newly enabled ordinary abilities, both backed by existing global mechanics coverage.
R3-80 Mega forms and Mega Stones remain a separate mega-beta-v4 extension so Mega forms never appear as recruitable base species.

Beta v25 marks every base species that currently owns a promoted Mega relation as content-complete: Venusaur, Blastoise, Beedrill, Charizard, Chesnaught, Scizor, Feraligatr, Meganium, Steelix, Camerupt, Heracross and Medicham.

The complete Mega-base union contains 274 legal Champions moves and 22 legal base-form Abilities; every relation is promoted into the active Training catalog only because mechanics coverage is supported in both Single and Double.
Schema v4 adds completeSpeciesIds as a fail-closed contract: removing even one legal move or Ability from a completed species invalidates the slice.
Mega validation now requires every promoted Mega relation to point at a recruitable base species that is present in completeSpeciesIds, preventing future Mega-only content promotion.

Beta v25 preserves every optional move/Ability/item already enabled by v24; full Mega-base relations are additive, yielding 285 active moves and 26 ordinary Abilities rather than regressing non-Mega beta options.

R3-82 promotes Alakazam, Aerodactyl, Garchomp, Gyarados, Ampharos and Manectric as content-complete Mega-first base species; every legal candidate move and base Ability is active and executable in Single/Double before the corresponding Mega relation is enabled.
Mega form data is reviewed separately in mega-beta-v5; Garchompite Z remains outside this wave so the classic Garchompite relation cannot be conflated with the distinct Mega Garchomp Z form.
R3-83 increases the Mega-first vertical batch to ten fully content-complete base species: Abomasnow, Absol, Altaria, Audino, Banette, Gallade, Gardevoir, Glalie, Houndoom and Lucario.

Every legal candidate move and base Ability for the ten Wave 6 species is promoted only because global mechanics coverage is executable in both Single and Double; Mega forms remain separate non-recruitable relations.

Wave 6 cross-checks Mega identity/stats/Ability against PokéBase Champions and explicit per-form height/weight against Pokémon Database; physical values are never inherited from the base form without review.
